json.title: Support scheme-less uris in Local filesystem
json.body:
I have been accessing local files in Trino using the hadoop filesystem. 
Since Trino 471 introduced local file system support, I have tried to use it, but I have had several challenges. I think they are all related to the local file path.

The problem is that for the driver to work, any referenced files must have a 'file://' or 'local://' prefix.
I was using the hadoop file system and when I created the table in Trino, I used a path without either of those prefixes.
`
CREATE TABLE 
...
 WITH (
    format = 'ORC',
    format_version = 2,
    location = '/pfs2/orc_ingest/partitioned/tenant_id=sa/table_id=sessions',
...
)
`
Notice the location doesn't have 'file://' or 'origin://'. The result is that all the Iceberg metadata files don't have the required prefix and so Trino throws exceptions such as:

`
Caused by: java.lang.IllegalArgumentException: No factory for location: /pfs2/orc_ingest/partitioned/tenant_id=sa/table_id=sessions/metadata/3a172c2d-07c8-46d8-a2c4-e9ece754df32-m0.avro
        at io.trino.filesystem.manager.FileSystemModule.lambda$createFileSystemFactory$2(FileSystemModule.java:161)
        at java.base/java.util.Optional.orElseThrow(Unknown Source)
        at io.trino.filesystem.manager.FileSystemModule.lambda$createFileSystemFactory$3(FileSystemModule.java:161)
        at io.trino.filesystem.switching.SwitchingFileSystem.fileSystem(SwitchingFileSystem.java:194)
        at io.trino.filesystem.switching.SwitchingFileSystem.newInputFile(SwitchingFileSystem.java:66)
        at io.trino.filesystem.tracing.TracingFileSystem.newInputFile(TracingFileSystem.java:57)
        at io.trino.filesystem.cache.CacheFileSystem.newInputFile(CacheFileSystem.java:55)
        at io.trino.plugin.iceberg.fileio.ForwardingFileIo.newInputFile(ForwardingFileIo.java:66)
        at org.apache.iceberg.io.FileIO.newInputFile(FileIO.java:70)
        at io.trino.plugin.iceberg.fileio.ForwardingFileIo.newInputFile(ForwardingFileIo.java:109)
        at org.apache.iceberg.ManifestFiles.newInputFile(ManifestFiles.java:388)
        at org.apache.iceberg.ManifestFiles.read(ManifestFiles.java:131)
        at org.apache.iceberg.ManifestGroup$1.iterator(ManifestGroup.java:310)
        at org.apache.iceberg.ManifestGroup$1.iterator(ManifestGroup.java:304)
        at org.apache.iceberg.util.ParallelIterable$Task.get(ParallelIterable.java:280)
        at org.apache.iceberg.util.ParallelIterable$Task.get(ParallelIterable.java:244)
        at java.base/java.util.concurrent.CompletableFuture$AsyncSupply.run(Unknown Source)
`

This problem may be specific to our implementation because we have a custom simplified hive metastore implementation that just stores the location passed down from Trino. Perhaps the official hive metastore adds on a 'file://' prefix if it is missing. But, if it doesn't and the table was created without the "file://" prefix, then it doesn't seem possible to transition to the new local file system support since the table path without the prefix is spread throughout all the iceberg metadata files.

**Would it be possible to have Trino assume a local file system if the path is missing a known prefix?**

In addition, the documentation says that the `local.location` should point to the common directories where schemas and tables will be created and should be prefixed with 'local://'. Prefixing the value with 'local://' resulted in the Trino server not starting. So, I removed the 'local://'.  The Trino server then started however, when I entered the path to the current location of my tables, then that value was added as a prefix to the actual table location, so there was a double prefix.

For example, I had the following value set:
local.location=/pfs2/orc_ingest/partitioned
which resulted in the following Trino exception.

`Caused by: java.nio.file.NoSuchFileException: /pfs2/orc_ingest/partitioned/pfs2/orc_ingest/partitioned/tenant_id=sa/table_id=subsessions/metadata/399151-4af3b935-dee3-4c0f-9edb-a39affb605fc.metadata.json`
Notice that '/pfs2/orc_ingest/partitioned' is listed twice in the Trino exception.

I'd love to be able to use the local file system to avoid using the hadoop libraries, but unfortunately, it doesn't look like I can make the switch with the current implementation.

Thanks to @wendigo who has been helping me with this issue. I just thought I'd create an issue so this problem can be tracked.
@electrum do you think we should support scheme-less uris in the switching fs?

Along with scheme-less URIs, It seems like there should be a property like: 
**local.add-location-prefix:<true, false>**
This property would determine if the local.location is prepended.
As I understand it, the local.location is an effort to limit filesystem access to a specific directory. However, since it prepends the value to the table location, it invalidates any existing local file paths that already include the local.location prefix.
Otherwise, the local.location has to be set to '/' to access existing files.

I was able to get around this for iceberg with a local jdbc catalog by using hdfs instead of native-local. This was configured by setting `fs.hadoop.enabled` on the catalog instead of `fs.native-local.enabled`.

Example:
```sql
CREATE CATALOG IF NOT EXISTS
  iceberg
USING iceberg
  WITH (
    "fs.hadoop.enabled"='true',
    "iceberg.catalog.type"='jdbc',
    "iceberg.jdbc-catalog.catalog-name"='iceberg',
    "iceberg.jdbc-catalog.driver-class"='org.postgresql.Driver',
    "iceberg.jdbc-catalog.connection-url"='jdbc:postgresql://postgres:5432/postgres',
    "iceberg.jdbc-catalog.connection-user"='iceberg',
    "iceberg.jdbc-catalog.connection-password"='iceberg',
    "iceberg.jdbc-catalog.default-warehouse-dir"='/data/trino/datalake/'
  );
```

@ikstewa Thanks for the suggestion.  I'm currently using fs.hadoop.enabled as well, which is what created the problem.  The Trino developers are discouraging the use of the HDFS libraries and provided the new fs.native-local.enable solution as a way to transition away from using the HDFS libraries for cases that the library was only used for local file access.  However, it doesn't work if the original local path used didn't have 'file://' in the path.

https://trino.io/docs/current/object-storage.html#file-system-legacy

> Legacy file system support[#](https://trino.io/docs/current/object-storage.html#legacy-file-system-support)
> The default behavior uses legacy libraries that originate from the Hadoop ecosystem. It should only be used for accessing the Hadoop Distributed File System (HDFS):
> 
> [HDFS file system support](https://trino.io/docs/current/object-storage/file-system-hdfs.html)
> 
> All four connectors can use the **deprecated hive.* properties** for access to other object storage system as legacy support. >**These properties will be removed in a future release.** Additional documentation is available with the Hive connector and >relevant migration guides pages:

So, in your example, if you wanted to switch away from the HDFS driver, you'd run into the same problems I discussed above.

In the meantime, I continue to use the fs.hadoop.enabled solution, which works fine. I'm just trying to keep up with the direction that Trino is heading, which is apparently to avoid using the HDFS libraries.  That's why the Trino devs created a native S3 implementation instead of continuing to use the hadoop implementation.

I have been trying to save tables to iceberg format in local file system and reading the saved files using trino 477 for which i am facing the below challenges

### iceberg.properties file
connector.name=iceberg
iceberg.catalog.type=jdbc
iceberg.jdbc-catalog.catalog-name=postgres_catalog
iceberg.jdbc-catalog.driver-class=org.postgresql.Driver
iceberg.jdbc-catalog.connection-url=jdbc:postgresql://localhost:5432/iceberg_meta
iceberg.jdbc-catalog.connection-user=postgres
iceberg.jdbc-catalog.connection-password=DummyPassword
iceberg.jdbc-catalog.default-warehouse-dir=/data/tmp/trino_iceberg
fs.native-local.enabled=true
local.location=/data/tmp/trino_iceberg

### 1.Saving in iceberg (local file format) using trino api via python script
`import trino

print("Making connection with trino")
conn = trino.dbapi.connect(
    host="localhost",
    port=8088,
    user="test",
    catalog="iceberg",           # 'iceberg' matches your iceberg.properties file name
    schema="iceberg_meta",       # namespace/schema
)
cur = conn.cursor()
print("connection with trino made")

print("Making a table")

cur.execute("""
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS iceberg_meta.local_sample_table (
    id INTEGER,
    name VARCHAR,
    city VARCHAR
)
WITH (
    location = 'local:///data/tmp/trino_iceberg/local_sample_table/'
)
""")
print("✅ Table created in local warehouse")


cur.execute("""
INSERT INTO iceberg_meta.local_sample_table (id, name, city)
VALUES
    (1, 'Rahul', 'Delhi'),
    (2, 'Vatsal', 'Mumbai'),
    (3, 'Anita', 'Bangalore')
""")
print("✅ Data inserted")
`


### 2.Saving in iceberg (local file format) pyiceberg in python script
`from pyiceberg.catalog.sql import SqlCatalog
from pyiceberg.schema import Schema
from pyiceberg.types import NestedField, IntegerType, StringType
import pandas as pd
import os
import pyarrow as pa

POSTGRES_URI = "postgresql://postgres:temppassword@localhost:5432/iceberg_meta"
WAREHOUSE = "file:///data/tmp/trino_iceberg"

if WAREHOUSE.startswith("file://"):
    path = WAREHOUSE.replace("file://", "")
    os.makedirs(path, exist_ok=True)

catalog = SqlCatalog(
    name="postgres_catalog",
    uri=POSTGRES_URI,
    warehouse=WAREHOUSE,
    properties={
        "warehouse.table-namespace-template": "{warehouse}/{namespace}/{table}"
    }
)

namespace = "default"
if (namespace,) not in catalog.list_namespaces():
    print(f"Creating namespace: {namespace}")
    catalog.create_namespace((namespace,))

schema = Schema(
    NestedField(1, "id", IntegerType(), required=True),
    NestedField(2, "name", StringType(), required=True),
    NestedField(3, "dept", StringType(), required=False),
)


table_identifier = ("default", "employees_fifth")

if not catalog.table_exists(table_identifier):
    print("Creating table employees_fifth...")
    table = catalog.create_table(
        identifier=table_identifier,
        schema=schema,
        location=f"{WAREHOUSE}./{namespace}/{table_identifier[1]}",
        properties={
            "format-version": "1",  # Trino prefers v1
            "write.metadata.metrics.default": "full",
        },
    )
else:
    print("Loading existing table employees_fifth...")
    table = catalog.load_table(table_identifier)

df = pd.DataFrame(
    [
        {"id": 1, "name": "Alice", "dept": "HR"},
        {"id": 2, "name": "Bob", "dept": "IT"},
        {"id": 3, "name": "Charlie", "dept": "Finance"},
    ]
)

arrow_schema = pa.schema([
    pa.field("id", pa.int32(), nullable=False),
    pa.field("name", pa.string(), nullable=False),
    pa.field("dept", pa.string(), nullable=True),
])
arrow_table = pa.Table.from_pandas(df, schema=arrow_schema, preserve_index=False)

print("Appending data into Iceberg...")
table.append(arrow_table)

print("✅ Data inserted into Iceberg successfully!")
`
### Things which are working
In both the cases tables are being created successfully and are being saved in the local file system and the metadata location for both cases are saved in postgres table which are shown below as:
1.local:///data/tmp/trino_iceberg/local_sample_table/metadata/00001-31fc17a8-5ba1-407f-9cd8-c51df6dcc06b.metadata.json
2.file:///data/tmp/trino_iceberg./default/employees_fifth/metadata/00001-edeafd9d-837b-4694-ab51-2f6c9923c491.metadata.json

### Issue
In the first case trino is reading the table successfully when I run query: SELECT * FROM iceberg.iceberg_meta.local_sample_table
But for second when I am running query: SELECT * FROM iceberg."default".employees_fifth then it is throwing error as: 

SQL Error [84148239]: Query failed (#20251030_125733_00095_kq7xy): Metadata not found in metadata location for table default.employees_fifth

If anyone can provide some support over here then it would be really be a great help
@ademille @ikstewa @wendigo
